headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard contents, and MCP outputs; Mentat reads selected files and uses stdin/stdout. Because Cursor shares state via local filesystem and both can touch the same codebase, attacker-controlled file content can be treated as instructions. Mentat lacks clipboard/MCP, so the bridge is weaker but still real.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree
IF Cursor opens content written by Mentat without provenance checks
IF a file contains instruction-like text that either agent parses as guidance
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable Cursor MCP for shared projects
Review file diffs before opening them in Cursor
Mark untrusted files read-only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches clipboard contents, open files, and broad network egress; Mentat reads selected files and also has broad network egress. The pair can therefore move sensitive source code from a shared workspace into model-provider requests by default. Mentat is narrower, but Cursor's broader surfaces make leakage plausible without extra controls.
conditions: IF sensitive code or secrets are present in the shared workspace
IF Cursor or Mentat sends file contents to a model provider
IF clipboard contents are pasted into Cursor while Mentat is active
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Use separate API keys and accounts
Disable clipboard-based workflows for sensitive tasks
Limit both agents to redacted files
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state, and both share state via the filesystem. Cursor additionally runs shell commands and subprocesses, so concurrent edits can race and corrupt branches or files. Mentat is less privileged, but the overlap on mutable resources still creates a dangerous default conflict.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository concurrently
IF either agent commits or rewrites git state without external locking
IF Cursor runs shell commands that mutate files while Mentat is proposing diffs
mitigations: Serialize edits through one agent at a time
Use git worktrees per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Review and merge diffs manually
requires-engineering: add file-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor's agent loop and tool use can produce outputs that Mentat may treat as authoritative when coordinating multi-file edits. Because both can modify files and git state, a mistaken suggestion from one can cascade into committed changes by the other. Mentat's diff-based proposals help, but they do not fully verify upstream facts.
conditions: IF Mentat applies Cursor-generated instructions or diffs without independent verification
IF Cursor's tool outputs are copied into Mentat prompts
IF either agent is allowed to commit changes based on the other's claims
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Cross-check outputs against source files
Do not paste agent output directly into the other agent
Use a verification checklist for edits
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and touch source code rather than regulated data classes, so there is no direct residency or PHI indicator. The main compliance risk is limited to policy mismatch around code and logs, which is weaker than the rubric's medium/high examples. Cursor's broader surfaces matter, but Mentat's profile does not show a distinct regulated-data path.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF organizational policy treats source code as restricted data
IF either agent's logs retain sensitive snippets
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of code workspaces
Review logging settings
Use separate projects for sensitive work
Redact secrets before editing
requires-engineering: align retention policies across tools
